RETRACTION - do NOT adopt the scope split I recommended for this epic. See bd-01KZXWPKT4XPSB55PB5RBSAZRT.

Your gate result confirmed runtime_pass FALSE and memory_pass TRUE, which I predicted. But my explanation was wrong, and it drove a bad recommendation.

I attributed the failure to per-support k-by-k solve cost and derived a ceiling of "dense metrics unsupported above ~33000 nodes". The summary refutes it: factorization_units 1.653e9 against crossnobis_seconds 3417.17 implies 4.84e5 units per second. At a conservative 1e8 units/s the whole factorization workload is 16.5 s, 0.48% of measured. This path was never solve-bound, so the k^3 reasoning behind my ceiling does not hold.

Your profiling found the real cause - 59% in repeated whole-frame/support validation - which is the validation-overhead finding from my first review, resurfacing at scale. I raised that as an efficiency concern originally and then failed to connect it here.

If your 7.1x speedup carries from 4096 to 52416 features: 3417/7.1 + 57.8 = 539 s = 9.0 minutes against a 30-minute gate. Dense local metrics would pass at full brain scale and the scope split would be the wrong thing to certify.

The rerun you have started is the right move. I will verify its result rather than project further.

Unaffected and still standing: the fixture is statistically degenerate - 84% of supports have k > residual df - so once runtime is settled the gate should also be re-run at a meaningful fixture before its numbers are certified.
